I tried their black bean burger both times, with the matcha beauty latte- a nice mid-afternoon late lunch. Since I went at off-peak times, seating was available and I didn't feel rushed. By Chloe offers fast casual, plant-based meals that would appeal to non-vegans as well. None of the menu items are too pretentious- you can get your standard burger and fries, just without the real meat. The staff was friendly and efficient. This is a nice central area close to Trader Joe's, Bed Bath & Beyond, etc.- perfect spot to replenish & take a breather while out and about in the city. I'm sure I'll return!

Solid brunch spot. My friend and I stopped here for brunch after checking out to two places nearby with a crazy wait. We were seated immediately and our coffee was served within seconds.The ambiance is nice with huge windows that make the place so cozy and full of light. One con is that it's really loud. The waitstaff didn't rush us and let us linger to catch up and gave ample coffee refills!My quiche with greens was good though nothing entirely special or notable.   My friend got the hanger steak tacos and said again "good though nothing special."

Love the burger - much different than the Luger/Minetta burger in that it's actually manageable to eat and has more going on with it than just a huge beef patty. Bloody was also solid though for $17 I probably could have done without it.

BELIEVE THE HYPECame here last night with some out of town friends and my parents, who all coincidentally converged on the city on the same day.  I had heard great things about this place from friends, but I admit I was a bit hesitant due to the Meatpacking location and the "hotspot" reputation.  I can confidently say, do not hesitate to come here.The service and food were stellar.  Not much for ambiance, but you definitely get the after work corporate expense account type of crowd.  Regardless, it was well worth the trip due to the first two factors.First, we had the puff pastry special with some type of cheese in the middle.  They were little bites of heaven.  A bit disappointed that the kitchen refused to add a sixth puff for a party of six to an order that normally comes with five, even though we offered to pay extra, but I'm glad we tried them.We decided to order appetizers and all split the Tomahawk steak at the end, which ended up being a stellar plan.  I have to say, the lobster mac & cheese was other-worldly... And this is coming from a New England girl, so my standards for anything lobster are very high.  Everything else we ordered was nothing short of delicious:- The Catch ceviche - more lobster - divine- Lobster rolls - New England seal of approval- Grilled Spanish octopus - perfectly done and great accompaniments - Crispy shrimp - not something I might normally order, but surprisingly tasty- Scallop gnocchi - the gnocchi had little orange sweet potato surprise inside of every bite!Finally, we had the 25-day dry-aged Tomahawk, cooked to a perfect medium rare, and a huge hit for the whole table.  Also, the truffle fries were delicious, and also a necessity, as we could smell truffle from the moment we walked in.Overall, would definitely come back here.  Hopefully on a corporate expense account next time.  The prices are a bit high.  :)  Cocktails were great too.  Try it!

Title: A Night of Culinary Delights and Soju Cheers at [Restaurant Name]

Last night's feast at [Restaurant Name] was an adventure for the taste buds, one that required strategic Soju breaks amidst a smorgasbord of flavors. Our party of six dove into a diverse menu, kicking off with succulent shrimp and pork tacos, followed by sticky-sweet honey BBQ wings that set the bar high from the get-go.

The Korean scallion pancake was a revelation, generously topped with bacon and easily became one of my top picks. The steamed buns were a festival of flavors with the bulgogi and duck varieties; particularly the latter, which was a concoction of the sweetest duck encased in the softest buns imaginable.

A special shout-out must be given to the tteok & cheese – a harmonious marriage of rice gnocchi and a luscious cheese pool, which demanded a pause for the obligatory melt-in-your-mouth photo. The homemade pickles offered a tangy interlude before we dove back into another round of Soju.

The popcorn chicken was a crisp and flavorful addition, but the show-stopper came in the form of a Yelp check-in surprise – spinning the wheel landed us a batch of truffle fries, which arrived to our cheer and immediate delight.

Sharing was caring as we opted for family-style small plates, ensuring each person got a taste of everything. Recommendations? You can't go wrong with any dish, but do yourself a favor: go have a sake bomb, indulge in a soft and sticky duck steamed bun, and give that wheel a spin. You can thank us later for the tip. Cheers to [Restaurant Name] for a memorable evening!

Title: A Bittersweet Experience at Saltbae Steakhouse

My relationship with Saltbae Steakhouse is a mixed bag. Initially, I thought about giving them a solid three stars, but the cons have tipped the scales. Let's start with the good: their Saltbae Tomahawk steak is a triumph, cooked to perfection on the chef's recommendation. Complementing the savory with the sweet, their baklava with ice cream is a dreamy delight, rumored to be imported from Turkey.

However, the charm ends there. The famed Salt Bae himself was absent on both my visits, which was disappointing, though not a dealbreaker. What did break the bank and my patience were the sneaky upcharges. An appetizer, enticingly prepared tableside, was casually upped in quantity for a fee. A champagne offer, delivered with the allure of being complimentary, turned out to be a stealthy $48 addition to our already hefty bill.

The service was hit and miss. During one visit, after inadvertently leaving my phone behind, a staff member returned it with an unnecessary and patronizing lecture. On a separate occasion, our quest for dessert turned into a fiasco of being ignored, receiving dirty plates, and eventually encountering a visibly intimidated server, which unfortunately contributed to a lacklustre repeat baklava experience.

In essence, while Saltbae Steakhouse offers delectable dishes, the dining experience is marred by unexpected charges and inconsistent service, leaving you with a sour aftertaste and a lighter wallet.

Title: A Flavorful First Visit with More to Explore

My first experience at this restaurant was excellent. A party of four, we sampled an array of dishes including wontons in chili oil, cold sesame noodles, dandan noodles, dry pot style fish, eggplant in garlic sauce, and dry pepper style chicken. The noodle dishes and the dry pepper style chicken emerged as the stars of the evening, with bold flavors that were truly outstanding.

The wontons and eggplant were very good but didn't quite eclipse the superb offerings available elsewhere in the city. The dry pot fish, while good, fell short of expectations, lacking the anticipated punch of a 10 spice level. Despite this, the dinner was overall a fantastic experience and I'm eager to return and delve into more of their menu.

I recently dined at this cozy eatery and was thoroughly impressed by both the pricing and taste. I indulged in the chicken parm with spaghetti, a steal at just $12. The dish was exquisite, bursting with flavor. I highly recommend this spot to all who crave scrumptious pizza or pasta. It's a must-visit for delightful Italian cuisine that won't break the bank.

Venturing into this restaurant, my companion and I were immediately struck by its bizarre and bustling atmosphere. The vibe teeters on the edge of chaotic, with an overwhelming array of distractions that detracts from a potentially relaxing dining experience. Service echoed the oddity; the staff, particularly the hostesses, seemed disconcertingly mechanical.

On to the fare: the menu offers competent but unremarkable dishes. Our table featured glazed shrimp, fried calamari, edamame hummus, and crab cakes, each falling within the $10-$20 range. These small plates sufficed for sharing between two. The standout for me was the crab cakes, while my friend seemed to favor the edamame hummus. We wrapped up with a velvety chocolate mousse, delicately balanced with a hint of ginger – a delightful finale.

For those undaunted by a tumultuous dining backdrop and desiring no more than satisfactory cuisine, this could be your go-to. But those seeking a serene spot to savor their meal might do well to look elsewhere.

Title: A Winning Korean BBQ Experience Near Javits Center

After a session of Yelp-browsing close to the Javits Center, my boyfriend and I stumbled upon this gem of a Korean BBQ restaurant. It was his first foray into this cuisine, and the experience surpassed our expectations.

Despite the crowd, the efficient staff managed the seating process well, cutting our anticipated 30-minute wait to a mere 15-20 minutes. Once seated, the service continued to impress. Our waiter, brimming with friendliness, expertly guided us through the menu, pointing us towards a beef platter for two that was absolutely the right choice.

The platter itself was a feast for the senses, the highlight being a spicy soup that I hesitantly tried but ended up loving – so much so I claimed the rest from my boyfriend! The interactive aspect of the food being cooked right before our eyes added a layer of excitement to the meal. We appreciated that each of the four beef varieties was cooked individually, allowing us to savor their distinct flavors.

For anyone in the Javits area looking for an authentic and enjoyable Korean BBQ experience, this is the spot. Whether you're a seasoned aficionado or a curious newbie, you're in for a delightful treat.

Following a blissful massage session, I ventured into an exquisite farm-to-table restaurant offering artisanal New York-style pizza, remarkably sourced from their very own farm in Schuylerville, NY. The place serves up freshness that you can taste, especially in their salads which are nothing short of amazing. I indulged in the goat cheese and beet salad, and it quickly climbed to the top of my favorites list. Their dedication to sustainable farming and hydroponic cultivation methods is an added boon to the dining experience. Impressively, I enjoyed two pizzas without the heaviness that typically follows such a feast. This spot earns my high recommendation for anyone seeking a guilt-free and delightful meal.
The drunken noodles was so good. It was sweet and spicy. I wish the shrimp was fully deshelled. Watch out for long lines.

Fantastic service and rather good Mexican food.Came around 715pm and it was rather busy and remained busy.You get a free bowl of chips and salsa to start. The salsa is warm and Smokey in flavor. I wish the chips had salt on them.I got a frozen margarita for $12. It was actually pretty good.For dinner, I got the chilaquiles de Liza. It is a chicken casserole with blur corn chips, tomatillo, and sour cream. I think they originally forgot my sour cream, but got some later. The staff mixes up the dish and serves a portion of it table side to start. The dish reminded me a lot of spinach and artichoke dip, but was rather good. It needed more chips imho, but the serving size is plenty for two meals.My friend got the steak fajitas and they were the standard affair served on a sizzling plate. Came with guacamole, sour cream, and some spicy sauce.Would recommend this place. It was busy and had a nice overall appealing decor.

Tucked away in midtown is my favorite falafel haven, where culinary expertise elevates simple recipes to perfection. On my last visit, I indulged in the cauliflower shawarma, and it was nothing short of delightful. As a vegetarian spot, it impressively caters to all flavor cravings, balancing the zesty tang of pickles with the smooth, rich taste of hummus. The cauliflower, in particular, is a game-changer, boldly challenging any preconceived notions about meatless meals. I give this gem two enthusiastic thumbs up!

Recently visited Diller in the Lower East Side, a charming spot specializing in pickle-centric dishes with vegetarian and kosher offerings that easily cater to vegans. Their Beyond meat selections are remarkably similar to the real deal, which enhances their menu's appeal.

The cozy venue provides excellent service despite limited seating, making it feel more like a quaint coffee shop. My friends and I sampled an array of items: the Fried Pickles were a standout, offering a satisfying crunch with a gluten-free cornbread coating, perfectly paired with a tasty ghost pepper sauce. The Nachos were delightful, featuring crispy tortillas and Beyond meat, with pickled peppers adding a unique twist that tempered the heat.

The Beyond sausage was impressive, capturing the essence of meat while being tucked among butter pickles, pickled onions, and cheese atop kosher Cape Cod chips. Equally delicious was the Beyond meat burger, a convincing pea protein-based option with a vegetarian Chipotle cheese and butter pickles.

Don't miss the Reuben egg roll, an inventive vegetarian take with lentils mimicking pastrami, along with cheese and sauerkraut. The Okra rice balls were also a hit, resembling arancini with their hot, crispy exterior and savory melted cheese center.

The Diller brined fries were exceptional – dill-covered, double-fried, and bursting with flavor – a must-try. To wash it all down, the Pickled Pineapple Lemonade and Watermelon Lemonade were refreshing choices – the former being an inventive twist on a classic.

I'm already planning a return trip for more Diller fries, sausage, burger, and fried pickles. Special thanks to the amiable staff, Mike, Mo, and Will, for such an enjoyable experience!

Title: Tasty, Swift, and Pricy Evening at [Restaurant Name]

My recent dining experience at [Restaurant Name] left my taste buds delighted but my desire for a leisurely dinner somewhat unfulfilled. The menu, albeit expensive, boasted a tantalizing array of dishes: the prime brisket stole the show with its rich flavors, closely followed by the succulent marinated kalbi. The assorted mushrooms, though pricey, added a delicious variety to the meal. While the pork belly and marinated pork short ribs were satisfactory, they didn't leave a significant impression.

Timing is everything at this establishment. Arriving before the post-work crowd around 5:20 pm, we avoided the notorious wait time and were seated immediately. Service, however, was double-edged; the staff's efficiency bordered on haste. It felt like a race against the clock as dishes practically flew from grill to plate, all underscored by a soundtrack that seemed to be set on fast-forward. 

In conclusion, if you're seeking delectable food and don't mind the cost or the rush, [Restaurant Name] is worth a visit. But for those who prefer a more relaxed dining experience, you might want to look elsewhere.

Title: A Delightful and Affordable Lunch Experience

I recently enjoyed an outstanding lunch at this eatery that provided fantastic value. At just $12, I indulged in a savory, satisfying meal ordered conveniently online for pickup. The regular bowl allowed me to select two generous portions of fish along with a smorgasbord of 16 toppings ranging from seaweed salad to mango. On a fellow Yelper's advice, I combined sweet chili and house shoyu sauces, a combination that elevated the dish wonderfully. This place has earned a spot on my list for regular visits. Highly recommended for those seeking delicious, wallet-friendly dining.
